advances: Tests propagation from a critical boundary profile, even after a normal-weighted interior centroid calibration. The normalized depth is $13/36$, above the conjectured threshold.

proof:
Writing a base as $z_i=t_i-t_0$ in the barycentric coordinates of the base triangle shows that if an integer coordinate is negative the point is $v_0$; otherwise the nonnegative integer coordinates sum to at most one. This gives exactly $P$. The three cap margins sum to zero. Cap $j$ takes its strict full outer fiber at $v_j$, neither other outer fiber, and a homothetic central cap of area $4V/9$. Hence they cover the ambient space with masses $13V/9$. Their central sections have centroid $g$ because $\lambda_j=1/3$ there and the other two coordinates average to $1/3$; the three coarea masses with the given unnormalized margins agree by barycentric permutations preserving area. Thus the equal response weights are $1/3$.

To check every normal at $(0,g)$, move the threshold of a containing halfspace to that point. Its margin has form $a\cdot z+u\cdot(x-g)$. The central trace has mass at least $4V/9$ by 6769574fc1bd9f8d with retained mass $V$ (if $u=0$, the whole central fiber is captured). Couple uniform points on the outer triangles by cycling the barycentric coordinates of one uniform point. Their sum is $3g$, and $\sum_j v_j=0$, so the three coupled margins sum to zero. At least one is captured in every triple, and each marginal is uniform, proving outer captured mass at least $V$. This establishes the exact all-normal depth. At any point with a positive selected margin, a small increase in that threshold still contains the point and removes a positive-area strip on the proper central section, giving lower depth. Any point with no positive margin has all three zero. Since the offsets are integers and $0\le\lambda_j\le1$, all offsets must be zero, giving $(0,g)$. This proves uniqueness.

On an edge of length $L$ use its affine parameter $r\in[0,1]$. Write $U$ and $U_{\rm mid}$ for uniform probabilities on the whole interval and its middle third. The outer source law at each outer base is $(12L/13)U$; the central law is $(12L/13)U+(4L/13)U_{\rm mid}$. The target is $LU$ at every base. Keep each outer source fixed. From the central uniform component retain $(9L/13)U$ identically at base zero and send $(L/13)U$ to each outer base at unchanged parameter. The conditional base mean is zero. For the central middle component write $r=(1+s)/3$ with $s$ uniform on $[0,1]$, keep the base, and send it with equal probabilities to $(s+j)/3$, $j=0,1,2$. The conditional mean parameter is $r$, and the target is uniform. This constructs the target law, preserves the continuous normal on each edge, and preserves the row barycenters even when source components overlap. Endpoints are null. The central surplus over target is $3L/13$ on each edge and thus $3\sigma/13$ in total. The base squared norm is zero centrally and sums to $4$ over the three outer bases, each of which has target minus source mass $\sigma/13$.

The weight $h_{K-g}(n)=(x-g)\cdot n>0$ is constant on each edge and the row's normal is preserved, so weighting preserves barycenters. The divergence theorem applied to $x-g$ and to each component of $x$ times $x-g$ gives $\int_{\partial K}(x-g)\cdot n\,dS=2V$ and $\int_{\partial K}x((x-g)\cdot n)\,dS=2Vg$. Each outer outgoing part is one thirteenth of this weighted boundary law, with continuous mean $g$. The full indicator of $K$ is a retained density of mass $V$ at its centroid, which also has projective energy $V$ by d90ba05577427854. The uniqueness already proved excludes the outer marks.
statement: Let $v_0=(-1,-1)$, $v_1=(1,0)$, $v_2=(0,1)$ and $P=\{0,v_0,v_1,v_2\}$. For a nondegenerate triangle $K$ of area $V$, centroid $g$ and perimeter $\sigma$, the mixed set of $\operatorname{conv}(P)\times K$ is $P\times K$ and its unique deepest mixed point is $(0,g)$, of raw depth $13V/9$ and normalized depth $13/36$. Put $\ell(z)=(-z_1-z_2,2z_1-z_2,2z_2-z_1)$, $H_j=\{\lambda_j(x)-1/3+\ell_j(z)\ge0\}$ for the barycentric coordinates of $K$, and $W=\frac13\sum_j\mathbf1_{H_j}$. If $\eta$ is the actual sum of boundary arclengths with continuous outward normals attached, there is a normal-preserving martingale from $\nu=(36/13)W\eta$ to $\eta$. Every coupling with these marginals sends at least $3\sigma/13$ of the central boundary source mass to other bases, and $\int|z|^2\,d(\eta-\nu)=4\sigma/13$. After weighting the exhibited coupling by $h_{K-g}$ on the shared normal, the continuous mean of its outgoing part to each outer base is $g$. These three centroid marks have the same ordinary retained mass and projective energy as $(0,g)$, namely $V$, but are not mixed deepest.
title: An actual critical boundary martingale must leave the unique deepest fiber
